scope: Theorem 5.1 (Alias extraction) of the manuscript “Subset Sum in Time $`O(2^{0.49n})`$” (preprints/Subset-Sum-in-Time-2-power-0-49n-October-4-2026/subset-sum.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 138 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 69f9398e325a2628), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is one randomized procedure with the following properties for all sufficiently large n. Its input consists of the transformed integers ci = Cai + ui and targets ts = Ct + s, 0 ≤ s ≤ nN0, of (2.1), with the input-length guard (5.1). It chooses P uniformly from [2⌊ηn⌋, 21+⌊ηn⌋) among the primes and returns either failure or P together with a deduplicated list of genuine aliases for each target. If E|V |=⌊n/2⌋d(V ) ≤ .01004n, then, with probability 1 − o(1) over P and the remaining random choices, it does not fail and its lists equal As(P) simultaneously for every s. The error bound is uniform over the transformed inputs satisfying these assumptions. For every outcome of its random choices, the procedure stores and visits at most 2⌈τn⌉ poly(n) records, where τ = .48996, and takes 2τn poly(n + b + 2) elementary bit operations, apart from the implementation of exact uniform finite draws. Those draws admit the bounded implementations in Section 6.
